# Chapter One

The Library of Alexandria stood near the harbor of the ancient city. Eratosthenes,
a librarian there, calculated the circumference of the Earth using the angle of
shadows cast at noon in two different cities on the same day.

# Chapter Two

Centuries later, the library was lost. Hypatia, a teacher at the museum, kept the
mathematical traditions alive even as the city's politics became hostile.

# Chapter Three

The story of Alexandria is the story of two scholars: Eratosthenes, the methodical
geographer who measured the world by counting shadows, and Hypatia, the philosopher
who taught long after the city's golden age had ended.
